question: Answer in short bullet points, "unknown" if unsure. (1) CAPTIONS: font style, size relative to frame, vertical position, words per screen, case, outline; which words (if any) get a different colour or size and WHY (the number, the conflict word, a name, or random); does any caption pop or animate in? (2) FIRST 2 SECONDS: what is on screen in frame 1, what is the first spoken line, is there movement, is text on screen. (3) VOICE: pace (fast/medium/slow), pauses between sentences, emphasis changes. (4) SFX: list each sound effect type (whoosh, hit, riser, pop...) and approximately when. (5) MUSIC: genre, volume vs voice, any drop before the payoff. (6) VISUAL DEVICES: zoom/punch-ins, speed ramps, freeze frames, circles/arrows, split screens; how many cuts per 10 seconds. (7) LAST 2 SECONDS: what happens and does it loop to the start.
answer:
Here is the breakdown based on the video:

* **CAPTIONS:**
  * **Style & Font:** Clean modern sans-serif (e.g., Montserrat/Proxima Nova), bold, white font with a soft black drop-shadow/outline.
  * **Size & Position:** Medium size, centered vertically around lower-middle/chest level (hook header at 0:00–0:02 sits near the top).
  * **Words Per Screen:** Short chunks, roughly 2–5 words per frame.
  * **Case:** Standard sentence case (hook title at the start uses uppercase for emphasis: *"BOTH TEAMS"* and *"WON!"*).
  * **Color / Emphasis:** Subtitles remain consistent white text without color shifting; dedicated bold graphic callouts pop on-screen for stats (e.g., *"26 POINTS A GAME"*, *"12 REBS PER GAME"* at 0:09–0:12).
  * **Animation:** Instant cut/pop per phrase timed tightly to the voiceover.

* **FIRST 2 SECONDS:**
  * **Frame 1:** NBA game footage of Matthew Dellavedova wrapping up Bradley Beal on a drive.
  * **First Spoken Line:** *"NBA trades where both teams thought they won!"*
  * **Movement:** Fast-paced game motion of Beal falling back while Dellavedova fouls him.
  * **On-Screen Text:** Title text at top: *"NBA trades where BOTH TEAMS thought they WON!"*

* **VOICE:**
  * **Pace:** Fast-paced, dynamic sports commentary/creator style.
  * **Pauses:** Very brief, punchy micro-pauses between sentences to keep viewer retention.
  * **Emphasis:** Pitch lifts on key players (*"LeBron James"*, *"Kevin Love"*), numbers, and punchlines.

* **SFX:**
  * **0:01:** Referee whistle / court squeak during the foul.
  * **0:05, 0:12, 0:22:** Subtle swoosh / whoosh transitions for team logos.
  * **0:09, 0:11:** Pop / slide-in hits for stat overlays.
  * **0:14, 0:29, 0:31, 0:36, 0:40:** Comedic timing pauses and subtle whooshes/hits for inserted meme clips (IShowSpeed, Homelander, Vince McMahon, Pakistani fan, crying meme).

* **MUSIC:**
  * **Genre:** Low-key instrumental hip-hop / trap beat.
  * **Volume:** Low in the background under the voiceover; slightly ducked or cut during quick comedic reaction cuts.
  * **Drop:** Brief pauses/drops coinciding with reaction memes before resuming the narrative rhythm.

* **VISUAL DEVICES:**
  * **Framing / Elements:** Vintage CRT TV graphic framing game highlights; pop-up team logos (Cavaliers, Timberwolves); bold graphic stat trackers; cutaway reaction memes (IShowSpeed, Homelander, Vince McMahon, crying meme).
  * **Camera Movement:** Subtle push-ins/punch zooms on talking heads and player stills.
  * **Cut Frequency:** Very rapid—around 4–5 cuts every 10 seconds.

* **LAST 2 SECONDS (01:05–01:07):**
  * **Visual:** Andrew Wiggins in Warriors championship attire hugging the Larry O’Brien trophy with his eyes closed in joy.
  * **Spoken Line:** *"...because he did it for Golden State."*
  * **Loop:** Does not create an endless audio/visual loop; it concludes on a definitive punchline ending.
